key_insight: Recursive, weight-sharing transformers can outperform over-parameterized surrogates in small engineering datasets by shifting capacity from learnable parameters to reusable computation.
engineering_relevance: For semiconductor thermo-mechanical reliability workflows, these models offer a practical way to replace costly repeated FEA with faster surrogate predictions while staying within tight memory and compute budgets.
method: Compare three recursive transformer variants: Tiny Recursive Model, Depth Recursive transformer, and a simple recursive transformer.
Evaluate predictive performance alongside parameter count and FLOPs to quantify the accuracy–efficiency trade-off.
Validate on two low-dimensional tasks: semiconductor package thermo-mechanical reliability and a Laplace PDE capacitance solver.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a hardware-aware comparison on two low-dimensional engineering prediction tasks using Recall, Mean Reciprocal Rank, parameter count, and FLOPs as evaluation signals.
watch_item: Recursive architectures still need careful tuning and validation, because compute savings can come with architecture-specific training instability or limited gains if the surrogate task is not truly data-scarce.
paper_title: Recursive transformers for semiconductor thermo-mechanical reliability
